source: Ha! ha! ha! ha! hem! clear my throat!—I’ve been thinking over it ever since, and that ha, ha’s the final consequence. Why so? Because a laugh’s the wisest, easiest answer to all that’s queer; and come what will, one comfort’s always left—that unfailing comfort is, it’s all predestinated. I heard not all his talk with Starbuck; but to my poor eye Starbuck then looked something as I the other evening felt. Be sure the old Mogul has fixed him, too. I twigged it, knew it; had had the gift, might readily have prophesied it—for when I clapped my eye upon his skull I saw it. Well, Stubb, wise Stubb—that’s my title—well, Stubb, what of it, Stubb? Here’s a carcase. I know not all that may be coming, but be it what it will, I’ll go to it laughing. Such a waggish leering as lurks in all your horribles! I feel funny. Fa, la! lirra, skirra! What’s my juicy little pear at home doing now? Crying its eyes out?—Giving a party to the last arrived harpooneers, I dare say, gay as a frigate’s pennant, and so am I—fa, la! lirra, skirra! Oh—
We’ll drink to-night with hearts as light, To love, as gay and fleeting As bubbles that swim, on the beaker’s brim, And break on the lips while meeting.
A brave stave that—who calls? Mr. Starbuck? Aye, aye, sir—(Aside) he’s my superior, he has his too, if I’m not mistaken.—Aye, aye, sir, just through with this job—coming.

modern_en.title: Chapter 39 — First Night-Watch
paragraphs: Ha! Ha! Ha! Ha! Ahem! Let me clear my throat! I've been thinking about it ever since, and that ha, ha is the final conclusion. Why? Because a laugh is the wisest, easiest answer to everything that's strange. And come what may, one comfort always remains — that unfailing comfort is, it's all predestined. I didn't hear all his talk with Starbuck, but to my poor eye, Starbuck looked then something like the way I felt the other evening. You can be sure the old Mogul has got him, too. I caught on, I knew it — if I'd had the gift, I could easily have prophesied it — because when I clapped my eye on his skull, I saw it. Well, Stubb, wise Stubb — that's my title — well, Stubb, what of it, Stubb? Here's a carcass. I don't know all that may be coming, but whatever it is, I'll go to meet it laughing. What a mischievous leer lurks in all your horrors! I feel funny. Fa, la! Lirra, skirra! What's my juicy little pear at home doing now? Crying its eyes out? Giving a party for the latest harpooners to arrive, I'd wager, as cheerful as a frigate's pennant, and so am I — fa, la! Lirra, skirra! Oh —
We'll drink tonight with hearts as light, To love, as gay and fleeting As bubbles that swim on the beaker's brim, And break on the lips while meeting.
A brave song that — who calls? Mr. Starbuck? Yes, yes, sir — (Aside) he's my superior, and he has his too, if I'm not mistaken. — Yes, yes, sir, just finishing this job — coming.

modern_da.title: Kapitel 39 — Første Nattevagt
paragraphs: (Stubb alene, i færd med at reparere en bras.)

Ha! Ha! Ha! Ha! Hm! Lad mig få renset struben! Jeg har tænkt over det lige siden, og det ha, ha er den endelige konklusion. Hvorfor? Fordi et grin er det klogeste og letteste svar på alt, hvad der er mærkeligt. Og hvad der end sker, er der altid én trøst tilbage — den bundsolide trøst er, at det hele er forudbestemt. Jeg hørte ikke hele hans snak med Starbuck, men for mit stakkels øje lignede Starbuck dengang lidt det, jeg selv følte forleden aften. Du kan være sikker på, at den gamle Mogul har fået fat i ham også. Jeg kunne se det, jeg vidste det — havde jeg haft evnen, kunne jeg let have spået det — for da jeg kastede øjnene på hans kranium, så jeg det. Nå, Stubb, kloge Stubb — det er min titel — nå, Stubb, hvad så, Stubb? Her er et ådsel. Jeg ved ikke alt, hvad der kan komme, men uanset hvad det er, går jeg det i møde med et grin. Sikke et drillende grin der gemmer sig i alle dine rædsler! Jeg har det så løjerligt. Fa, la! Lirra, skirra! Hvad mon min saftige lille pære derhjemme laver nu? Græder den øjnene ud af hovedet? Holder den fest for de nyeste harpunerer, der er kommet, skulle jeg mene, lige så glad som en fregats vimpel, og det er jeg også — fa, la! Lirra, skirra! Åh —
Vi drikker i nat med hjerter så lette, Til kærlighed, lystig og flygtig som bobler, der svømmer på bægerets rand og brister på læben, når de mødes.

En tapper sang, den der — hvem er det, der kalder? Mr. Starbuck? Ja, ja, sir — (Til sig selv) han er min overordnede, og han har også sit, hvis jeg ikke tager fejl. — Ja, ja, sir, jeg er lige færdig med det her arbejde — jeg kommer.
